## Setup
```{r}
# Loading packages
library(terra) # raster handling
library(tidyverse)
library(tmap) # map making
library(kableExtra) # table formatting
library(spData) # spatial data
library(spDataLarge) # spatial data
library(geodata) # spatial data
library(sf)
```


```{r}
# Shapefile for the West Coast EEZ 

ez_data <- st_read("data/wc_regions_clean.shp")

# Bathymetry Raster 

bathymetry <- rast("data/depth.tif")
```

```{r}
#SST rasters (combine SSt rasters into a raster stack)

ann_avg_sst_2008 <- rast("data/average_annual_sst_2008.tif")
ann_avg_sst_2009 <- rast("data/average_annual_sst_2009.tif")
ann_avg_sst_2010 <- rast("data/average_annual_sst_2010.tif")
ann_avg_sst_2011 <- rast("data/average_annual_sst_2011.tif")
ann_avg_sst_2012 <- rast("data/average_annual_sst_2012.tif")

# test class of raster objects
class(ann_avg_sst_2008)
```

```{r}
# Combine rasters into a stack 
raster_stack <- c(
    ann_avg_sst_2008, 
    ann_avg_sst_2009, 
    ann_avg_sst_2010, 
    ann_avg_sst_2011, 
    ann_avg_sst_2012)
```


```{r}
#Checking the CRS 
st_crs(ez_data) == st_crs(bathymetry)
st_crs(ez_data) == st_crs(raster_stack)
st_crs(bathymetry) == st_crs(raster_stack)

```

##Process data
Next, we need to process the SST and depth data so that they can be combined. In this case the SST and depth data have slightly different resolutions, extents, and positions.
```{r}
# find the mean SST from 2008-2012 (e.g. create single raster of average SST)

sst_mean <- mean(raster_stack, na.rm = TRUE) 
print(sst_mean)

```

```{r}
# convert average SST from Kelvin to Celsius hint: subtract by 273.15
sst_celsius <- (sst_mean - 273.15)
print(sst_celsius) 

# crop depth raster to match the extent of the SST raster 
cropped_depth <- crop(bathymetry, sst_celsius)
```

```{r}
# note: the resolutions of the SST and depth data do not match resample the depth data to match the resolution of the SST data using the bilinear method approach check that the depth and SST match in resolution, extent, and coordinate reference system hint: can the rasters be stacked?


resampled_depth <- resample(cropped_depth, sst_celsius, method = "bilinear")

# Vverify matching
cat("After resampling:\n")
cat("Resolutions match:", all(res(resampled_depth) == res(sst_celsius)), "\n")
cat("Origins match:    ", all(round(origin(resampled_depth), 8) == round(origin(sst_celsius), 8)), "\n")
cat("Extents match:    ", ext(resampled_depth) == ext(sst_celsius), "\n")


```

## Find Suitable Locations 
- To find suitable locations for marine aquaculture, we’ll need to find locations that are suitable in terms of both SST and depth.
- reclassify SST and depth data into locations that are suitable for oysters
-  hint: set suitable values to 1 and unsuitable values to 0
- find locations that satisfy both SST and depth conditions

```{r}

# Define a reclassification matrix
sst_rcl <- matrix(c(-Inf, 11, 0, # unsuitable 
                11, 30, 1,  # suitable 
                30, Inf, 0), # unsuitable
              ncol = 3, 
              byrow = TRUE)

# Apply the matrix to reclassify the raster, making all cells 0 or 1 or 2
sst_suitability <- classify(sst_celsius, rcl = sst_rcl, right = FALSE) 

```



```{r}
# Reclassify depth for oysters

depth_rcl <- matrix(
  c(
    -Inf, -70, 0,  # Unsuitable
    -70, 0, 1,     # Suitable
    0, Inf, 0      # Unsuitable
  ),
  ncol = 3,
  byrow = TRUE
)

# Project and resample depth to match SST raster
depth_projected <- project(
  resampled_depth,
  sst_celsius,
  method = "bilinear"
)

# Reclassify projected depth raster
depth_suitability <- classify(
  depth_projected,
  rcl = depth_rcl,
  right = FALSE
)

# Check that CRS matches
same.crs(sst_suitability, depth_suitability)

# Combine the rasters
suitable_zones <- c(
  sst_suitability,
  depth_suitability
)

# Multiply suitable zones to find suitable locations
suitable_locations <- lapp(
  suitable_zones,
  fun = function(sst, depth) sst * depth
)

```


##Determine the most suitable EEZ
- We want to determine the total suitable area within each EEZ in order to rank zones by priority. To do so, we need to find the total area of suitable locations within each EEZ.

```{r}
# select suitable cells within West Coast EEZs
eez_rast <- rasterize(ez_data, suitable_locations, field = "rgn_id")

# find area of grid cells
cell_size <- cellSize(suitable_locations, unit = "km")

# Only want the suitable cells 
suitable_area <- suitable_locations * cell_size

# find the total suitable area within each EEZ
# hint: it might be helpful to rasterize the EEZ data

# Calculate suitable area by EEZ
eez_suitable <- zonal(
  suitable_area,
  eez_rast,
  fun = "sum",
  na.rm = TRUE
)

# Rename suitable area column
eez_suitable <- eez_suitable |>
  rename(
    suitable_km2 = lyr1
  )

# Join suitable area to EEZ polygons
ez_summary <- ez_data |>
  left_join(eez_suitable, by = "rgn_id")

# Check results
head(ez_summary)
```

## Oyster Map Creation 
```{r}
# Map creation

oyster_map <- tm_basemap("OpenStreetMap") + 
  tm_shape(ez_summary) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "suitable_km2",
    fill.scale = tm_scale_continuous(
      values = "brewer.blues"
    ),
    fill_alpha = 0.6,
    fill.legend = tm_legend(
      title = "Suitable area (km2)",
      position = tm_pos_out("right", "center")
    ),
    col = "black"
  ) +
  tm_graticules() +
  tm_scalebar(position = c("left", "bottom"), text.size = 0.7) + 
  tm_compass(position = c("right", "top")) +
  tm_title("Oyster Suitability Analysis for West Coast EEZs", size = 1.5)


# Display map
oyster_map
```


Oyster Map Interpretation: The oyster map shows suitable habitat across the West Coast EEZs, primarily Southern California and parts of Washington State. Based on the selected criteria, these regions have the most potential for oyster aquaculture success.

## Suitability for the Pacific Calico Scallop 

- sealifebase link: https://www.sealifebase.ca/country/CountrySpeciesSummary.php?Country=US+America+%28contiguous+states%29&genusname=Argopecten&speciesname=ventricosus


```{r}

# Suitability for the Pacific Calico Scallop

# Pacific calico scallop suitability parameters
# Depth range: 0-180 meters below sea level

# Reclassify SST for Pacific calico scallop

scallop_sst_rcl <- matrix(
  c(
    -Inf, 21, 0,       # Unsuitable
    21, 31, 1,         # Suitable
    31, Inf, 0         # Unsuitable
  ),
  ncol = 3,
  byrow = TRUE
)

scallop_sst_suitability <- classify(
  sst_celsius,
  rcl = scallop_sst_rcl,
  right = FALSE
)

# Project and resample depth to match SST raster

scallop_depth_projected <- project(
  resampled_depth,
  sst_celsius,
  method = "bilinear"
)

# Reclassify depth for Pacific calico scallop

scallop_depth_rcl <- matrix(
  c(
    -Inf, -180, 0,    # Unsuitable
    -180, 0, 1,       # Suitable
    0, Inf, 0         # Unsuitable
  ),
  ncol = 3,
  byrow = TRUE
)

scallop_depth_suitability <- classify(
  scallop_depth_projected,
  rcl = scallop_depth_rcl,
  right = FALSE
)

# Check that CRS matches

same.crs(
  scallop_sst_suitability,
  scallop_depth_suitability
)

# Combine the rasters

scallop_suitable_zones <- c(
  scallop_sst_suitability,
  scallop_depth_suitability
)

# Multiply suitable zones to find suitable locations

scallop_suitable_locations <- lapp(
  scallop_suitable_zones,
  fun = function(sst, depth) sst * depth
)


# Select suitable cells within West Coast EEZs

scallop_eez_rast <- rasterize(
  ez_data,
  scallop_suitable_locations,
  field = "rgn_id"
)

# Find area of grid cells

scallop_cell_size <- cellSize(
  scallop_suitable_locations,
  unit = "km"
)

# Only want the suitable cells

scallop_suitable_area <-
  scallop_suitable_locations * scallop_cell_size

# Calculate suitable area by EEZ

scallop_eez_suitable <- zonal(
  scallop_suitable_area,
  scallop_eez_rast,
  fun = "sum",
  na.rm = TRUE
)

# Rename suitable area column

scallop_eez_suitable <- scallop_eez_suitable |>
  rename(
    suitable_km2 = lyr1
  )

# Join suitable area to EEZ polygons

scallop_summary <- ez_data |>
  left_join(scallop_eez_suitable, by = "rgn_id")

# Check results

head(scallop_summary)
```

## Scallop Map Creation 
```{r}


# Map creation

scallop_map <- tm_basemap("OpenStreetMap") + 
   tm_shape(scallop_summary) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "suitable_km2",
    fill.scale = tm_scale_continuous(
      values = "brewer.blues"
    ),
    fill_alpha = 0.6,
    fill.legend = tm_legend(
      title = "Suitable area (km²)",
      position = tm_pos_out("right", "center")
    ),
    col = "black"
  ) +
  tm_graticules() +
  tm_scalebar(position = c("left", "bottom"), text.size = 0.7) +
  tm_compass(position = c("right", "top")) +
  tm_title(
    "Pacific Calico Scallop Suitability Analysis for West Coast EEZs", 
    size = 1.5
  )

# Display map

scallop_map

```


Scallop map interpretation: The Pacific Calico Scallop Suitability Map shows that there is no suitable habitat across the West Coast EEZs based on the selected temperature and depth criteria.
